_why: THE NAMED SET. Doctrine #4: every negative has a positive control. Twenty-five
tests in this tree declare themselves one; until now they were twenty-five tests
that happened to exist, with no record of WHICH refusal each one controls for.
A positive control whose negative nobody wrote down is a test that looks like
rigour and proves only that something passes.
Each entry pairs a positive control with at least one negative it stands beside,
and states the property the pair establishes together. test_positive_control_set.py
asserts every entry resolves to a real collected test, and — the half that keeps
this honest — that every self-declared positive control in the tree is registered
here, so the set cannot fall behind the code.

controls.property: expiry refuses a stale approval without refusing a live one
a failed record write stops the runtime and leaves no partial state, while a successful one proceeds
lock identity refuses an aliased store without refusing legitimate recovery
replay is refused on a live database while a current approval still executes
an unreadable mount row refuses only when it is on the resolution path
topology resolution refuses what it cannot see without refusing what it can
an empty range over NO substrate refuses, while the same empty range over a real one is clean (OPEN-GAPS G5)
substrate policy refuses an unsafe filesystem without refusing a safe one
the probe answers on a real checkout and reports unknown rather than safe when it cannot read
advisory evidence cannot satisfy a requirement that authoritative evidence can
a wrapper stays useful as calibration while never satisfying
the bank fails closed on a missing tier without refusing a covered action
a rollback is caught by chronology, and differing stamps are not a false alarm
the pin guard reports a wrong pin and not a right one, within its stated blind spot
re-resolution rejects a weakened snapshot and mints for an unweakened one
partial weakening is caught, not only wholesale weakening
the descriptor binds an assessment to its own target and attempt without refusing that binding
the TTL boundary is inclusive and an unswept expiry still refuses
rotation refuses a hold pinned to a superseded policy without refusing one whose policy has not moved
the mutation harness reddens under a mutation and is green without one
the platform gate converts off Linux and is inert on it
nine matrix rows refuse and the tenth genuinely authorizes (the _ROW_KIND mapping)
an incomplete response is refused and a complete one parses
credentials are wrapped everywhere without becoming unreachable where they are needed
plaintext transport is refused without refusing a working endpoint
a breached bound changes the verdict while an unbreached one still returns real verdicts in both directions (OPEN-GAPS G21)

a bare zero is refused at load while the NAMED unbounded posture still loads and still widens — without this the refusal is equally consistent with unbounded having been removed outright (OPEN-GAPS G21)
the collector that maps fields to their proofs can say no — an instrument returning an empty set would make the coverage guard vacuous for every field at once (doctrine #8, OPEN-GAPS G17)

the container adapter omits --memory under UNBOUNDED while still emitting the exact cap it was given — without the positive, the absence is equally consistent with an adapter that never caps memory at all (PR #106 P1)
the namespace adapter resolves UNBOUNDED to 0 at its argv line and still passes a real cap through unchanged
the unsafe adapter sets no RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_CPU under UNBOUNDED and sets the exact ones it was given otherwise
the adapter collector can say no — an empty set would make the class-level ratchet vacuous for every adapter at once (doctrine #8)
the class-level sweep for a finite number derived from an unbounded cap looks in the right place — the same assertions on a BOUNDED Limits must find those numbers
the attestation records the posture the run actually had, and does not say 'unbounded' for every configuration

the positional sweep refuses a narrowed population and does NOT refuse a healthy tree — without the positive, both refusals are consistent with an instrument that refuses everything and is merely useless rather than dishonest
the composition checker refuses a report with the right counts and the wrong membership, and an empty one, while accepting a faithful report (PR #106 review, item 1)

the implementation registry refuses a misspelled permitted name at construction, and an empty registry distinctly under its own reason, while a declared name constructs and its requirement is satisfied by that implementation's evidence (G26)

a declared site that is missing or reports another identity is refused at the declaration (class in hand) or at first use (path), while a declaration whose site reports the identity resolves and satisfies its requirement (G26, PR #111 review)

the pre-approval comparison refuses a branch that moved, and halts on a target that is wholly or partly unreadable, while an unchanged branch records the approval and reaches the executor (re-observation phase 1)

the pre-execution re-read refuses a target that moved after approval and makes the hold terminal rather than retry-eligible, while an unchanged target still executes on the same path (re-observation phase 1)
the exemption check finds a comparison call when one is there, so an empty intersection means the exempt services really decide nothing rather than the scan being blind
a registry that does not observe the pinned class refuses the approval, while a registry that does observe it still approves — the refusal is about the mismatch, not about the hold
the shipped factory's wiring refuses a target that moved without refusing approval itself
a supplied service is refused only when the registry beside it would be discarded, not for being supplied at all
a deployment that wires no re-observation is untouched by the discard refusal — nothing was requested, so nothing was discarded
the factory refuses a base branch that disagrees with the supplied reader, and one that is missing entirely, without refusing the combination when the two agree
a receipt found under the pre-upgrade subject is marked as an attribution, and one found under the current subject is not — so the marker distinguishes the two rather than appearing on both
the composition-time validator refuses bases the tool would not read without refusing the ones it would — so the refusal is about usability, not about naming a base at all
the executor refuses a candidate that never started without refusing one that did — including one the wall clock killed after it started, whose side effects really happened
the git reads and the branch-delete executor refuse a command that never ran without refusing one that did — so the merge proof is still produced when git actually executes
the branch-name predicate refuses every name git refuses without refusing the names git takes — so tightening it did not simply stop accepting anything

the reads refuse every name the tool's own predicate refuses without refusing the names it accepts — so routing classify, rev and the delete executor through is_usable_branch_name closed the second definition rather than stopping the reads from working
the AST allowlist pinning _BRANCH_RE to one function is reaching the source it scans — an allowlist that found nothing to look at would pass for the same reason a clean one does (doctrine #8)

the tls_reason guard still refuses everything outside the symbolic alphabet while G38 holds it at exactly one trailing newline — without it, a pin that records a gap is indistinguishable from a guard that has stopped refusing anything at all
a real human decision is chained, matches its row, and retry still executes once — so the decision binding refuses forged and altered decisions without refusing genuine ones
a real execution's outcome is chained with executed, detail and the structural start signals, and the row matches it — so the receipt verifier flags rewritten rows without flagging honest ones
every writer exercised on an honest ledger verifies clean — so the per-field detection parametrised over the derived record is not a verifier that flags everything

the reconcile gate's prefix match really does trip on execution.observation (the named G40 limit) while G39's outcome.execution, named outside the prefix, decodes cleanly — so the limit is a measurement and the event name is a decision, not luck

the three refusals are findings rather than a floor: on a ledger whose rows all have their receipts the same reader returns the row and the verdict is VALID, so 'refused' in the negatives above is caused by the unreceipted or rewritten row and not by the guard refusing everything it is asked

the undecodable-ledger refusals are caused by the malformed JSON column and not by the guard refusing every ledger: without the corruption the same verify_chain, the same reader and the same verify_receipts return their ordinary answers and verify_ledger_file is ok

narrowing the guard to the decoder's own exception did not stop the two threshold readers working: on the same clean ledger a real threshold still returns its rows, so the ValueError the negative observes is the caller's bad argument surfacing as itself rather than the readers refusing everything they are asked

the six hiding-shape refusals are caused by the component being hidden from the credited walk, not by the guard refusing any graph containing a substrate policy: the SAME defect in a container the walk credits is refused for the property it violates instead, naming allow_unverified_substrate rather than component_not_discovered
